JZTXs are a group of Janus-faced toxins that can be used to investigate the structure and function relationship of sodium channels and to develop new drugs.

JZTX is an effective inhibitor of NaV1.2, NaV1.3, NaV1,4, and NaV1.6, with a preference for NaV1.5 and NaV1,6, and that the bioactive surface is composed of three conserved hydrophobic residues and two conserved cationic residues.

the molecular surfaces of peptide toxins are critical for the understanding of their interaction with their target receptors, and the identification of their bioactive surfaces will facilitate the rational design of novel drugs.
